deep.reconstruction:
The page inventories special configurations of 5 marked points on the Riemann sphere, i.e. special points of M_{0,5}(C) for K = a 5-element label set. It records how S_5 = Aut(K) and complex conjugation σ act on them, and it is drawn as a graph whose edges carry incidence numbers. This belongs to the 1983 project of describing the Teichmüller tower in low dimension (M_{0,5} is the source of the pentagon relation), with explicit symmetric base points and paths.

Indexing and counting. Each family is indexed by a combinatorial 'structure' on K. G = Aut^+ is the stabilizer in S_5 of holomorphic automorphisms. G~ is the stabilizer once antiholomorphic maps are allowed, i.e. inside S_5 x {1,σ}. The subscript i is |G|, so each S_5-orbit has 120/i elements.

Level 2: the orbifold points of M_{0,5}.
- I_10, pentagonal: a regular pentagon on the equator. There are 12 = 4!/2 dihedral orders on K; G = D_5, G~ = D_5 x {1,σ}.
- I_6, bitetrahedral: an equilateral triangle J on the equator plus the two poles ω, with ω identified with the two orientations of J. There are 10·2 = 20; G = S_3.
- I_4, pyramidal: an oriented square plus an apex P. There are 5·3·2 = 30; G = Z/4.

Level 1: three families of 60, 60 and 120.
- II_2, square-right triangle: 'pentagon with a vertex', parametrized by (π ∈ Pent(K), s ∈ K).
- II'_2 = Tw_{1/4} II_2: obtained by twisting one hemisphere a quarter turn.
- II_1, tetrahedron-triangle: 'épingle' (pin) structures, K = J ⊔ E with |J| = 3, |E| = 2, ω an orientation of J and r ∈ J x E, giving 10·2·6 = 120. G = 1, G~ = {1,σ}.

Level 0: three families of 60, 120 and 60.
- III_2, triple right triangle: indexed by (π, ρ ∈ Rep π), and {(π,ρ)} ≅ Rep(K).
- III_1, triple semi-skew triangle: 120 épingle structures.
- III'_2, triple skew triangle: an oriented square with codiagonal plus a point P, giving 60 with G = Z/2.

Totals: 62 + 240 + 240 = 542.

Edges. Arrows between families are named maps or paths: f_{B,s}, f_{Q,α}, γ_{π,s}, γ'_{π,s}, γ_{π,ρ}, γ^1_r, γ^{1'}_r, γ^2_r, τ_{π,s} = tw_{1/4}, τ_{π,ρ} = tw_{1/4}, and τ^∘_r = tw_{1/6}. Each arrow carries a pair of valences that satisfy the double-counting identity N_A·a = N_B·b:
- I_6 to I_4 via f: 20·3 = 30·2.
- II_2 to I_10 via γ_{π,s}: 60·1 = 12·5.
- I_4 to II'_2 via f_{Q,α}: 30·4 = 60·2.
- III_2 to III_1 via τ_{π,ρ}: 60·2 = 120·1.
- III_1 to III'_2 via τ_r: 120·1 = 60·2.
- III'_2 to I_4 via γ^2_r: 60·1 = 30·2 (reading 1 at III'_2 and 2 at I_4).
Several edges are marked 'compatible with σ'.

What the graph is. The picture is an S_5 x Gal(C/R)-equivariant graph in M_{0,5}(C). Its vertices are highly symmetric, mostly real configurations, i.e. points fixed by an antiholomorphic involution; all except I_4 are real ('Sauf I_4, toutes ces structures sont réelles'). Its edges are real-locus arcs (γ, f) and fractional twists of a hemisphere (τ = tw_{1/4}, tw_{1/6}). In effect it is a choice of 542 symmetric base points with explicit connecting paths: a combinatorial model or groupoid presentation of π_1(M_{0,5}) with its S_5 action. This is part of the program announced in Esquisse d'un programme of presenting the Teichmüller tower (and the Galois action on it) through the first two levels.
errors: For I_4 (square pyramid) the page writes G~ = G = Z/4Z. If G~ is the stabilizer in S_5 x {1,σ}, the square-pyramid configuration has antiholomorphic symmetries: reflections in vertical planes, composed with a relabeling of the square. G~ would then be dihedral of order 8 (C_4v), not Z/4. Grothendieck's remark that I_4 is not 'real' is correct, since the five points are not cocircular, but that only shows (1,σ) is not in G~. Possibly G~ is defined differently, so this is unsure.
Minor notational slips: γ^1 is labelled with π but parametrized by r ∈ Rep(K); 'Q = Carr(K)' should read Q ∈ Carr(K); the order of G for III'_2 is written 'Z/2Z*'.
The level counts are internally consistent: 120/i gives 12, 20, 30, 60, 60, 120, 120, 60 and the total 542. The quoted incidence pairs also satisfy double counting. No arithmetic errors were found.

ideas.what: Classification of points of M_{0,5}(C) with nontrivial S_5-stabilizer: regular pentagon (D_5), bitetrahedral triangle plus poles (S_3), square pyramid (Z/4), with counts 12, 20, 30.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S_5 (finite subgroups of PGL_2 permuting 5 points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (finite subgroups of SO(3)); folklore in the moduli literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5} and the pentagon in the Teichmüller tower, but not this list explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Using the real structure: each special configuration has a group G~ inside S_5 x Gal(C/R), and almost all chosen base points are real points of some real form.
ideas.modern_name: Real points / real forms of M_{0,n}; Galois-equivariant base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Real moduli M_{0,n}(R): Kapranov, Devadoss (1990s); arithmetic use of real or tangential base points: Deligne, Ihara (1989 onward)

ideas.what: Equivariant graph of 542 special base points in M_{0,5} joined by real arcs and fractional hemisphere twists (tw_{1/4}, tw_{1/6}), with consistent incidence numbers, as a combinatorial model for the fundamental groupoid with S_5 action.
ideas.modern_name: Lego / Teichmüller groupoid presentation of π_1(M_{0,5}) with many base points; cell-type decomposition of M_{0,5}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Bakalov–Kirillov; Drinfeld (pentagon in GT); Moore–Seiberg
ideas.where_published: Programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this concrete graph is not published as far as I know

missed.claim: A complete S_5 x Gal(C/R)-equivariant inventory of 542 symmetric, mostly real, configurations of 5 points on P^1, linked by named paths with incidence numbers. It is a blueprint for presenting the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,5} with symmetric base points instead of tangential ones. Later GT literature works almost exclusively with tangential base points at the boundary (Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps). This interior-symmetric-base-point model seems not to have been developed or published.
missed.quote: niveau 2 I_10, I_6, I_4 ... niveau 1 II_2, II'_2, II_1 ... niveau 0 III_2, III_1, III'_2 ... 542 ... NB Sauf I_4, toutes ces structures sont "réelles"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Symmetric interior base points carry large automorphism groups (D_5, S_3, Z/4). That could give a presentation of GT-type actions or of the mapping class groupoid with built-in finite-order elements, and a real-structure-compatible version. The pentagon relation could then be seen via the D_5 orbifold point.

missed.claim: The twisting maps τ = tw_{1/4}, tw_{1/6} are fractional Dehn twists, i.e. finite-order rotations of a hemisphere. They connect real loci of different real forms (II_2 to II'_2, III_2 to III_1). This links the orbifold torsion of the mapping class group of the 5-punctured sphere with the gluing of real moduli components.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to studies of the real locus of M_{0,n} (Devadoss, Etingof–Henriques–Kamnitzer–Rains) and to how finite-order elements generate the Teichmüller groupoid. The explicit gluing data could be checked against those works.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, internally consistent combinatorial model (542 vertices with incidence numbers, real and Galois structure) of M_{0,5} with symmetric base points, made in 1983 for the Teichmüller tower program. The individual facts (orbifold points of M_{0,5}, real structures) are classical, and the general program is announced in the Esquisse. The specific equivariant graph appears unpublished but is a notable detail rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: '(Q=Carr(K), α∈Λ(Q)' is better read as (Q ∈ Carr(K), α ∈ Λ(Q)), and f_{Q,α} carries an arrow, f_{\vec Q,α}.
For III'_2, G is written 'Z/2Z*' (an asterisk or correction mark), not plain Z/2Z.
In II_2: 'K ≃ B ⊔ ω' (B possibly a bitetrahedral/pentagon datum), then 'P ∈ J et ω ≃ ω' = B∖{P}'; the reading is uncertain.
The 'γ_r^{2'}' label sits beside the tw_{1/6} loop on II_1; 'γ_r^2 compat. avec σ' labels the arrow between II'_2 and II_1.
'4 sommets' under II'_2 replaces a crossed-out word.
